mainTopic: Why מילה overrides שבת and צרעת: the refuted קל וחומר, the words "ביום" and "בשר", the source for a בינוני, and רב אשי's timing rule for עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא's קל וחומר that מילה overrides שבת. The גמרא explains why the תנא backed away with "או אינו": maybe שבת is stricter than צרעת, or maybe a מצורע is simply unfit for the עבודה. So the source for מילה on שבת is the word "ביום". A second ברייתא teaches that מילה overrides the ban on cutting off צרעת, and that the source is the extra word "בשר" in "ימול בשר ערלתו". רבא gives two versions of why that ברייתא first leaned on logic and then dropped it. One version uses a קל וחומר from שבת. The other uses עשה דוחה לא תעשה. The גמרא then asks how we know the law for a בינוני, a boy past the eighth day but not yet an adult. אביי answers with a הצד השוה, and רבא answers with a קל וחומר, which רב ספרא challenges. רב אשי ends with a key rule: an עשה overrides a לא תעשה only when the מצוה is done in the same act that breaks the prohibition. The amud closes as the גמרא begins a comment on the רבא and רב ספרא debate, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Completing the chain of logic that מילה overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is completed: עבודה overrides שבת, and מילה overrides צרעת, which itself overrides עבודה. So מילה should certainly override שבת, since שבת is pushed aside even by עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עבודה overrides שבת, and מילה overrides צרעת. If שבת gives way to the עבודה, isn't it logical that מילה overrides it too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out the תנא's original proof that מילה overrides שבת. It is built as a ladder of "who beats whom".
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the ברייתא said צרעת beats עבודה: a מצורע cannot do the Temple service. Here two more links are added: עבודה beats שבת, and מילה beats צרעת, because you may cut off a נגע on the ערלה. Since מילה beats the thing that beats עבודה, it should easily beat שבת, which even עבודה beats.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service (קרבנות)
Overrides / pushes aside
Circumcision
Is it not logical? (the opening of a קל וחומר)
Biblical leprosy; one may not cut off its signs

steps.confusionAlert: Track the ladder carefully: צרעת > עבודה > שבת, and מילה > צרעת. The phrase "מילה דוחה אותה" appears twice. The first time, "אותה" refers to צרעת. The second time, at the end of the step, it refers to שבת.

phrases.english: and the Temple service overrides Shabbat —
phrases.notes: The קרבנות of שבת are brought even on שבת.

phrases.english: yet circumcision overrides it (leprosy).
phrases.notes: You may cut off a נגע on the ערלה during the ברית מילה.

phrases.english: Shabbat, which is pushed aside by the Temple service,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁתְּהֵא מִילָה דּוֹחָה אוֹתָהּ?
phrases.english: is it not logical that circumcision should override it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת שֶׁנִּדְחֵית מִפְּנֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה, אֵינוֹ דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's קל וחומר earlier.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר built from the rankings among צרעת, עבודה, and שבת.

steps.title: Why did the תנא say "or perhaps not"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא added "או אינו" and doubted his own proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of "or perhaps not" that he said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא doubted his own proof. This question sets up the next steps, which explain the weakness in the logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After building the קל וחומר, the ברייתא said "או אינו" ("or perhaps not"), as if the proof might fail. The גמרא wants to know what flaw the תנא saw.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps not: a phrase that introduces doubt about a proof
That he said

phrases.english: And what is the "or perhaps not" that he said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the doubt the תנא raised against the proof in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness made the תנא doubt the קל וחומר.

steps.title: First flaw: maybe שבת is stricter than צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The תנא reconsidered. Who says צרעת is stricter than שבת? שבת has severe punishments and many warnings, so maybe it is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reconsidered and said: How do we know צרעת is stricter? Maybe שבת is stricter, since it carries punishments and many warnings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first reason the proof might fail. Maybe מילה can beat צרעת but not the stricter שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that beating צרעת is the harder task. But שבת carries כרת and סקילה and is warned about many times in the תורה. So beating צרעת does not prove that מילה can beat שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He reconsidered and said
Strict / severe
Punishments (כרת and סקילה)
Warnings (prohibitions)

phrases.english: He reconsidered and said:
And from where do we know that leprosy is stricter?
Perhaps Shabbat is stricter,
since it carries punishments
and many warnings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by showing a weak point in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ranking of צרעת above שבת is unproven, because שבת may be stricter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes צרעת is stricter than שבת.

steps.title: Second flaw: a מצורע is simply unfit for the service
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, maybe צרעת blocks עבודה not because it is strict, but because a מצורע is personally unfit to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: How do we know it is because leprosy is strict? Maybe it is because the man himself is not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to break the proof. This time it attacks the first link in the ladder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needed "צרעת beats עבודה" to mean that צרעת is a stronger law. But maybe a מצורע cannot serve only because of his personal status, since an unfit person cannot do the service. If so, צרעת never "beat" עבודה in strength, and the ladder falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively
The man / the person
Is not fit

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a second step in the same argument. It is an independent, alternative reason the קל וחומר fails.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
and from where do we know it is because leprosy is strict?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא מִשּׁוּם גַּבְרָא הוּא דְּלָא חֲזֵי.
phrases.english: Perhaps it is because the man is not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: וּמִמַּאי מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲמִירָא צָרַעַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate refutation alongside step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צרעת blocks עבודה because the person is unfit, not because the prohibition is stronger.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the reason is the strictness of צרעת rather than the unfitness of the person.

steps.title: Falling back on the פסוק: "ביום" means even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: With the logic broken, one might read "שמיני ימול" as excluding שבת. So the תורה adds "ביום" to teach that מילה is done even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would I apply "שמיני ימול"? Except on שבת. Therefore the verse says "ביום": even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the logic failed, the תנא proves the law directly from the extra word "ביום" in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the קל וחומר, "שמיני" alone could be read as "the eighth day, unless it falls on שבת". The word "ביום" ("on the day") points to that exact day no matter what, even on שבת. The final source is the פסוק, not logic.

keyTerms.meaning: And how do I apply (a verse)?
Therefore the verse says
On the day: the word that teaches "even on שבת"

steps.whatToRemember: מילה on the eighth day overrides שבת because of the word "ביום", not because of the קל וחומר, which was refuted in two ways.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for doing a ברית מילה on שבת when the eighth day falls then.

phrases.english: And how would I apply "on the eighth he shall be circumcised"?
Except on Shabbat.
Therefore the verse says: "on the day" —
even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic is refuted, the law is taken directly from the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מילה on the eighth day is performed even on שבת, based on "ביום".

steps.title: מילה overrides צרעת always, but יום טוב only on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that מילה overrides the ban on cutting off צרעת whether or not it is on the eighth day. It overrides יום טוב only on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: מילה overrides צרעת both in its time and not in its time. It overrides יום טוב only in its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a clear rule about when מילה overrides other laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between the two cases. Against צרעת, even a late מילה (after day eight) may cut off the נגע. Against יום טוב, only a מילה on the eighth day itself overrides it, because that permission comes from "ביום".

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (a ברייתא)
In its time: on the eighth day
Not in its time: a delayed מילה
A Festival

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Circumcision overrides leprosy,
both in its time and not in its time.
A Festival it does not override,
except in its time alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִילָה דּוֹחָה אֶת הַצָּרַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the scope of מילה overriding other laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה overrides צרעת at any time, but overrides יום טוב only on the eighth day.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of these rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rules. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above all, the גמרא wants to know how we know that מילה may cut a נגע despite the תורה's warning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that מילה overrides צרעת.

steps.title: "ימול בשר ערלתו": cut even with a בהרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the general phrase "ימול בשר ערלתו" means you cut the ערלה even if a בהרת is on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "ימול בשר ערלתו": even though there is a בהרת there, he should cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as allowing the cut even when a נגע is present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "ימול בשר ערלתו" is stated without conditions: the ערלה is cut, period. So even a בהרת on it does not stop the מילה. This phrase comes from ויקרא יב:ג, which speaks about the eighth day. Whether this source also covers a delayed מילה is asked in Step 19 and answered in Steps 20–21.

keyTerms.meaning: The flesh of his foreskin
A bright white spot: a sign of צרעת
He should cut it

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"The flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised",

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת,
phrases.english: even though there is a bright spot there,
he should cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 with a scriptural source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The open-ended phrase "ימול בשר ערלתו" permits cutting even where there is a בהרת.

steps.title: The warning about צרעת applies everywhere except the מילה
steps.stepSummary: The לאו of "השמר בנגע הצרעת" applies to all other places on the body, but not to the place of the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do I apply "השמר בנגע הצרעת"? In other places, except for the place of מילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the warning against cutting a נגע fits with the permission to cut it during מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "השמר" signals a לאו against cutting off a נגע. The ברייתא limits that לאו to the rest of the body, leaving the ערלה permitted. So the two פסוקים do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Take care: language that signals a לאו (prohibition)
A plague / leprous mark
In other places

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting a נגע is normally forbidden by "השמר בנגע הצרעת", but at a ברית מילה the ערלה is cut anyway.

phrases.english: And how do I apply "Take care with the plague of leprosy"?
In other places, except for circumcision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent clash between step 8 and the לאו of "השמר".
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לאו against cutting a נגע does not apply to the place of the מילה.

steps.title: Maybe the ban on cutting צרעת applies even at the place of מילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises another possibility: maybe the לאו of השמר בנגע הצרעת applies even to the ערלה. If so, "ימול בשר ערלתו" would only mean cutting when there is no בהרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it is not so, and the ban applies even to מילה. How then would I explain "ימול בשר ערלתו"? It would mean: when there is no בהרת on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own conclusion from Step 9 by suggesting the opposite reading. It is setting up the need for a stronger proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 the ברייתא said the לאו of צרעת does not apply at the place of מילה. Now it suggests reversing that: the לאו wins, and the מילה verse is limited to a clean ערלה. Both verses could fit either way, so one of them has to be narrowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only... (introduces the opposite possibility)
So how do I fulfill (explain) this other verse?
A bright white spot, a sign of צרעת
Foreskin

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is not so, but [the ban applies] even to the place of circumcision,
and how do I fulfill "the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised"?
— when there is no bright white spot on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 9 by flipping which verse is limited.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the לאו of צרעת does not apply at the place of מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two verses clash. Maybe the מילה verse should be the one that is limited, not the צרעת verse.

steps.title: The extra word "בשר" teaches that we cut even with a בהרת
steps.stepSummary: The תורה adds the word "בשר", which teaches that the ערלה is cut even if there is a בהרת on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says "בשר": even if there is a בהרת there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the opposite reading by pointing to an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ימול ערלתו" would have been enough. The extra word "בשר" means that whatever is on the flesh, even a בהרת, is cut along with it. So the מילה verse is not limited.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (an extra word gives a new lesson)
Flesh: the extra word in the פסוק

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "flesh,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת.
phrases.english: meaning even though there is a bright white spot there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which verse is limited: the מילה verse or the צרעת verse?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word "בשר" shows that מילה is done even with a בהרת.

steps.title: רבא is puzzled by the ברייתא's back-and-forth
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: at first, what was the תנא comfortable with, and in the end, what bothered him? The flow of the ברייתא seems to have no reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This תנא — what was acceptable to him at first, and what bothered him at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא questions the logic of the ברייתא itself, not the halacha. He wants to know why the תנא changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first said מילה wins without giving a reason. Then it said "או אינו" with no reason for doubting. Then it brought "בשר". רבא asks what the original reasoning was and what made the תנא abandon it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who analyzes the ברייתא
At first
It was acceptable to him
In the end

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי נִיחָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: This tanna — at first, what was acceptable to him,
and in the end, what was difficult for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי נִיחָא לֵיהּ וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to question the reasoning behind the whole ברייתא (Steps 9–11).
steps.kashyaTarget: The flow of the ברייתא: the first conclusion, then the "או אינו" doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No reason is given for the first view or for the doubt. The shift looks unexplained.

steps.title: The תנא first relied on a קל וחומר from שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the תנא first thought מילה overrides צרעת because of a קל וחומר: if מילה overrides strict שבת, surely it overrides צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: "ימול בשר ערלתו" — even if there is a בהרת. How do I explain "השמר בנגע הצרעת"? It applies to other places, not the place of מילה. Why does מילה override צרעת? It comes from a קל וחומר: if מילה overrides strict שבת, surely it overrides צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. He shows that the first part of the ברייתא was built on a קל וחומר from שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hidden reasoning was: שבת is very strict, yet מילה pushes it aside. So מילה should certainly push aside the less strict ban on cutting צרעת. That was what the תנא was comfortable with at first.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
"Take care with the plague of צרעת": the לאו against cutting off צרעת
A logical argument from a strict case to a lighter one
Overrides, pushes aside
All the more so

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
"The flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised" —
even though there is a bright white spot [there],
and how do I fulfill "take care with the plague of leprosy"?
In other places, except the place of circumcision.
But circumcision overrides leprosy.
What is the reason? It is derived from a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שַׁבָּת חֲמוּרָה, מִילָה דּוֹחָה אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: If Shabbat, which is stringent, is overridden by circumcision,
is it not all the more so with leprosy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of רבא's question: what the תנא accepted at first.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconstructing the hidden reasoning of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's first conclusion seemed to have no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first conclusion rested on a קל וחומר from שבת.

steps.title: Why the תנא doubted: maybe צרעת is stricter than שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the "או אינו": the תנא reconsidered. Maybe צרעת is stricter than שבת, because צרעת overrides עבודה and עבודה overrides שבת. That breaks the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the "או אינו" he said? He reconsidered and said: How do we know שבת is stricter? Maybe צרעת is stricter, since it overrides the עבודה, and the עבודה overrides שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the second half of his question: what bothered the תנא at the end. The תנא found a way to break the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if we are sure which side is stricter. Here there is a counter-chain: צרעת pushes aside עבודה (a כהן with צרעת cannot cut it off to serve), and עבודה pushes aside שבת. So צרעת may actually be stricter than שבת, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He reconsidered and said
Is stricter
Perhaps
The service in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The "או אינו" in the ברייתא is not a random new suggestion. רבא explains it as the moment the תנא saw that his קל וחומר could be broken.

phrases.english: And what is the "or perhaps not" that he said?
He reconsidered and said: From where do we know that Shabbat is more stringent?
Perhaps leprosy is more stringent,
since it overrides the Temple service,
and the Temple service overrides Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by explaining the doubt raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the ברייתא's change of mind as a refutation (פירכא) of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The "או אינו" seemed to be a doubt with no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt comes from a chain showing צרעת might be stricter than שבת, which breaks the קל וחומר.

steps.title: So the extra word "בשר" is needed
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר is broken, the תורה writes "בשר" to teach that מילה is done even when there is a בהרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says "בשר": even if there is a בהרת there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא's ending is now clear. The word "בשר" replaces the broken קל וחומר as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone could not prove that מילה overrides צרעת. So the rule must come from the extra word "בשר" in the פסוק. That answers the question from Step 7 about the source for מילה overriding צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though

steps.whatToRemember: מילה overrides the ban on cutting off צרעת. This is not learned from a קל וחומר from שבת, which is broken because צרעת overrides עבודה and עבודה overrides שבת. It is learned from the extra word "בשר" in "ימול בשר ערלתו".
steps.whyThisMatters: This follows the same pattern as the earlier steps about שבת: when a קל וחומר is broken, the תורה supplies an extra word to teach the rule directly.

phrases.english: Therefore, the verse teaches: "flesh" —

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת.
phrases.english: meaning even though there is a bright white spot there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the קל וחומר is broken in Step 14, the extra word "בשר" becomes the needed source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The extra word "בשר" is the source that מילה overrides צרעת, because the קל וחומר from שבת can be refuted.

steps.title: Second version: the תנא first relied on עשה דוחה לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: In רבא's second version, the תנא's first thought was that מילה overrides צרעת because an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: מילה overrides צרעת. What is the reason? Because an עשה comes and pushes aside a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's explanation of the ברייתא. It offers a different reason for the תנא's first idea that מילה beats צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 13), the first idea rested on a קל וחומר from שבת. Here it rests on a general rule instead: עשה דוחה לא תעשה. מילה is an עשה, and cutting off a צרעת spot is a לא תעשה, so the עשה should win.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version (of the same teaching)
A positive commandment, something you must do
A negative commandment, something you must not do
A positive מצוה comes and pushes aside a negative מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against Steps 12–15. It is the same רבא, retold with a different reason for the תנא's first thought.

phrases.english: Another version:
Circumcision overrides leprosy;
phrases.notes: This is the תנא's first thought.

phrases.english: what is the reason?
Because a positive מצוה comes and overrides a negative מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רבא's answer in Step 13, with a different reason for the תנא's first thought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate explanation of the ברייתא's flow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מילה overrides צרעת based on the general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is only the first thought; the next step shows why it falls apart.

steps.title: Why the תנא reconsidered: צרעת is an עשה and a לא תעשה together
steps.stepSummary: The תנא pulled back because the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה works only against a plain לא תעשה. Cutting off צרעת breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the 'או אינו' that the ברייתא says? He went back and said: Granted, we say an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה when it is only a לא תעשה. But this case involves both an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, the גמרא explains why the ברייתא says 'או אינו' (or perhaps not). The תנא found a weakness in his own first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה only beats a single, plain לא תעשה. Cutting off a צרעת spot breaks a לא תעשה ('השמר בנגע הצרעת') and also an עשה (רש״י: 'לשמור מאד ולעשות'). One עשה is not strong enough to push aside an עשה plus a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps not', the ברייתא's phrase for raising the opposite possibility
He went back and said, meaning he reconsidered
Alone, only by itself
A prohibition that has both a positive and a negative commandment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 14. There, the תנא pulled back because צרעת might be stricter than שבת. Here, he pulls back because צרעת carries an עשה plus a לא תעשה.

phrases.english: And what is the 'or perhaps not' that he says?
He reconsidered and said:
Say that we do say

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: that a positive מצוה comes and overrides a negative מצוה
only against a negative מצוה alone;
but this is a positive and a negative מצוה together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the reasoning given in Step 16, which explains the ברייתא's 'או אינו' in this version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ברייתא's reversal by limiting the scope of עשה דוחה לא תעשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any עשה pushes aside any לא תעשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עשה only pushes aside a plain לא תעשה, not an עשה plus a לא תעשה.

steps.title: So the פסוק 'בשר' is needed to teach that מילה overrides a בהרת
steps.stepSummary: Without the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה, one might limit מילה to a foreskin with no בהרת. The extra word 'בשר' teaches that the foreskin is cut even with a בהרת on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how do I explain 'ימול בשר ערלתו'? Only when there is no בהרת on it. That is why the תורה says 'בשר': even if there is a בהרת there.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the logical reason has fallen away, the ברייתא turns to the פסוק. The word 'בשר' proves that מילה is done even on a foreskin with a בהרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since logic alone no longer proves it, the halacha must come from a פסוק. The word 'בשר' is extra, so it adds a new teaching: cut the flesh even when a בהרת is there. The end result matches the first version (Step 15); only the route to get there differs.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I apply (this verse)?
The verse teaches (by saying)
Foreskin

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of רבא, the logical argument breaks down, so the extra word 'בשר' is what teaches that מילה overrides צרעת.

phrases.english: And how do I apply 'He shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin'?
When there is no white spot on it;
therefore the verse says 'flesh':

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת.
phrases.english: even though there is a white spot there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the logic of Step 16 was broken in Step 17, the ברייתא turns to the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מילה overrides צרעת because of the extra word 'בשר', not because of logic.

steps.title: The word 'בשר' covers a גדול and a קטן, but where is the source for a בינוני?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בשר' appears for an adult and for an eight-day-old. It does not appear for a boy in between, so where do we learn his law?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for an adult, since 'flesh' is written about him. It also works for a baby, since 'flesh' is written about him too. But for someone in between, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in the proof from 'בשר'. It asks for a source for a בינוני: a boy who was not circumcised on the eighth day and is not yet an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשר' appears in the פסוק about a גדול, who gets כרת. It also appears in the פסוק about a קטן on his eighth day. The פסוק about the בינוני ('המול לכם כל זכר') does not say 'בשר', so the derivation does not reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for this case)
An adult male who was never circumcised
A baby circumcised on his eighth day
In between: past the eighth day but not yet an adult
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: This works for an adult, since 'flesh' is written regarding him.
A baby too: 'flesh' is written regarding him.
An in-between child: from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the 'בשר' derivation from Step 18 reaches, and finds a case it does not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a בינוני's מילה also overrides צרעת.

steps.title: אביי derives the בינוני from what the גדול and the קטן share
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that neither the גדול nor the קטן alone can teach the בינוני, because each has a special feature. What they share, though, is that both are circumcised and both override צרעת. So every boy who is circumcised overrides צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It comes from the in-between. It cannot come from the adult alone, because he is punished with כרת. It cannot come from the baby alone, because his מילה is at its proper time. What they have in common is that both are circumcised and override צרעת. So too, anyone who is circumcised overrides צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by joining two sources together in a הצד השוה. He first shows why neither source works alone, then why together they do work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גדול is stricter because he gets כרת, so maybe only his מילה beats צרעת. A קטן is stronger because his מילה is בזמנה (it even beats שבת). Each special feature is cancelled by the other case. What is left is the shared point, that both are boys who need מילה, and that also applies to the בינוני.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from between them (by combining two sources)
Punished with כרת (spiritual cutting off)
מילה at its proper time, the eighth day
The common factor shared by two sources, used to learn a third case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the cases. 'From the קטן it can't come' does not mean the קטן is weaker. It means the קטן has an extra strength (בזמנה) that the בינוני lacks.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a בינוני's מילה overrides צרעת through a הצד השוה of the גדול and the קטן.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is derived from between them:
From an adult it cannot be derived,
since he is punishable by karet.
From a baby it cannot be derived,
since it is circumcision at its proper time.
The common factor between them
is that they are circumcised and override leprosy;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁנִּימּוֹלִין — דּוֹחִין אֶת הַצָּרַעַת.
phrases.english: so too, all who are circumcised override leprosy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הצד השוה from the גדול and the קטן teaches that a בינוני's מילה overrides צרעת.

steps.title: רבא: a קטן at the right time needs no פסוק, because of a קל וחומר from שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different approach. מילה on the eighth day overrides צרעת by a קל וחומר: if it overrides the stricter שבת, surely it overrides צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: מילה at its proper time does not need a פסוק to override צרעת. It comes from a קל וחומר: if it overrides שבת, which is strict, surely it overrides צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a different answer to the בינוני question. He first states that the קטן's case needs no פסוק at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה בזמנה already overrides שבת, which is very strict. So it must also override צרעת, which is lighter, and the קטן's case is covered by logic. That means the קטן's word 'בשר' is free to teach something else, which sets up how רבא will cover the בינוני.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not need a verse
Which is strict (more severe)
All the more so

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the setup for רבא's answer. If the קטן needs no פסוק, the extra 'בשר' written about him can be used for the בינוני instead.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ דּוֹחָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא,
phrases.english: That circumcision at its proper time overrides does not require a verse;
it is derived from an a fortiori argument:
If it overrides Shabbat, which is strict,
then leprosy, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ דּוֹחָה לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to אביי's הצד השוה for the question of Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה בזמנה overrides צרעת by a קל וחומר from שבת, without needing a פסוק.

steps.title: Maybe צרעת is stricter than שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רבא how he knows that שבת is stricter than צרעת. Perhaps צרעת is stricter, since it overrides עבודה, and עבודה overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to רבא: How do you know שבת is stricter? Maybe צרעת is stricter, since it pushes aside the עבודה, and the עבודה pushes aside שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks the starting point of רבא's קל וחומר. That argument needs שבת to be the stricter of the two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if you know which side is stricter. רב ספרא builds a chain: צרעת beats עבודה, and עבודה beats שבת, so maybe צרעת beats שבת. If so, the fact that מילה overrides שבת proves nothing about צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: more strict, more severe
the skin affliction described in the תורה, often translated 'leprosy'
the service in the בית המקדש
pushes aside, overrides

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Rava:
From where do we know that Shabbat is stricter?
Perhaps leprosy is stricter,
since it overrides the Temple service,
phrases.notes: A כהן with צרעת may not serve, even though the service is a מצוה.

phrases.english: and the Temple service overrides Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of רבא's קל וחומר from Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's assumption that שבת is stricter than צרעת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A chain of overriding (צרעת > עבודה > שבת) suggests צרעת may be stricter, which would undo the קל וחומר

steps.title: The מצורע is simply unfit to serve
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that צרעת keeps a כהן from serving because the man himself is unfit, not because צרעת is a stronger law.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is not because leprosy is stricter. It is because the man is not fit to serve.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his קל וחומר. He explains that צרעת does not really 'beat' עבודה in a contest of strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The service is not being pushed aside by a stronger law. This כהן was never eligible to serve while he has צרעת. So nothing here shows that צרעת is stricter than שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the man, the person
is not fit, not qualified

phrases.english: There, it is not because leprosy is stricter,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּגַבְרָא הוּא דְּלָא חֲזִי.
phrases.english: rather, it is because the man is not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the person is disqualified, rather than one law overriding another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צרעת overrides עבודה because it is a stricter law
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע is personally unfit, so no comparison of strictness can be drawn

steps.title: Why not cut off the spot and serve?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks why the כהן is unfit. Let him cut off his בהרת and then serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let him cut off his white spot and serve!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges רבא's answer. If the problem is only that the man is unfit, he could fix it by cutting away the spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting off צרעת breaks a לא תעשה, but the עשה of doing the service could override it. If the Torah still does not let him cut and serve, then צרעת really is pushing aside עבודה, and the question of strictness returns.

keyTerms.meaning: he should cut off
his bright white spot of צרעת

phrases.english: Why? Let him cut off his white spot and serve!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהן is merely unfit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The unfitness can be removed by cutting the spot, with the עשה of עבודה overriding the prohibition, so why isn't it?

steps.title: He still needs טבילה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even after cutting the spot, the כהן still needs טבילה before he may serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is lacking immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that cutting the spot would not let him serve right away. He must still immerse and wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא person must immerse and wait until nightfall before serving. So cutting the spot does not make him fit at that moment. Cutting would break the prohibition with no immediate gain, so it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: still lacking immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: He is lacking immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical obstacle: an additional requirement remains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting the spot would make him fit immediately
steps.terutzMaskana: He would still need טבילה, so cutting does not let him serve

steps.title: What about pure spots?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says the טבילה answer works for impure spots. But a pure spot needs no טבילה, so why can't that כהן cut it and serve?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for impure spots. For pure spots, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא shows that רבא's answer does not cover every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pure spot still disqualifies a כהן like a blemish, and cutting it is still forbidden. But no טבילה is needed afterward, so he could serve right away. The טבילה answer fails here.

keyTerms.meaning: it works out fine (for this case)
spots that make a person impure
spots that do not make a person impure, but still may not be cut off

steps.confusionAlert: Even a 'pure' spot is forbidden to cut off and stops a כהן from serving. 'Pure' only means it does not cause טומאה, so no טבילה is needed.

phrases.english: This works out for impure spots.
For pure spots, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 25 by pointing to a case it does not cover
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pure spots need no טבילה, so the obstacle רבא named is absent, yet cutting is still forbidden

steps.title: An עשה overrides only when done in the same act
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה only when the מצוה is done at the very moment the prohibition is broken. Cutting a spot only prepares the כהן to serve, so it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: When do we say an עשה comes and overrides a לא תעשה? In cases like מילה with צרעת, or ציצית and כלאים, where at the moment the לאו is broken, the עשה is fulfilled. Here, at the moment the לאו is broken, the עשה is not fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי drops the earlier answer and gives a new reason why the כהן may not cut his spot. This also defends רבא's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מילה, the cut that removes the צרעת is itself the מצוה. In ציצית with כלאים, attaching the strings is both the מצוה and the mixing. Cutting a spot to serve is only a step before the מצוה, so the עשה cannot override. That is why the כהן stays out, not because צרעת is stricter than שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a positive commandment overrides a negative one
at the moment, at the same time
the prohibition is uprooted (broken)
fulfills the positive commandment
woolen ציצית on a linen garment, a permitted mixture

steps.whatToRemember: עשה דוחה לא תעשה applies only when the מצוה is done in the same act that breaks the prohibition, not when breaking it merely prepares for the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This timing condition is a lasting rule for applying עשה דוחה לא תעשה throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Where do we say that a positive מצוה comes
and overrides a negative מצוה?
In cases like circumcision where there is leprosy,
or also tzitzis and kilayim,
where at the moment the prohibition is broken,
the positive מצוה is fulfilled.
Here, at the moment the prohibition is broken,
phrases.notes: Cutting a pure spot so the כהן can serve.

phrases.english: the positive מצוה is not being fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the טבילה answer, which failed in Step 26, with a new principle
steps.terutzResolutionType: New governing principle: the timing condition for עשה דוחה לא תעשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only obstacle to cutting and serving is the need for טבילה
steps.terutzMaskana: An עשה overrides a לא תעשה only when fulfilled at the same moment. Cutting a spot is only a preparation, so it is never allowed

steps.title: Introducing a remark on the רבא and רב ספרא debate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a comment about the dispute between רבא and רב ספרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this, the dispute of רבא and רב ספרא,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to say something about the רבא and רב ספרא exchange, and the rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא steps back from the back-and-forth to comment on the debate as a whole. The actual point will follow in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: and this (introducing a comment on what came before)

phrases.english: And this, the dispute of Rava and Rav Safra,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a comment on the whole exchange just completed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introductory formula only. The content continues on the next amud
